topic.title: Juniper Master Routing and Traffic Flow Troubleshooting
topic.scope: Defines the top-down diagnostic order across the entire network topology (L1 Access Switches, L1/L2 Aggregation Routers, and L2 PE/P/BNG Core Nodes).

troubleshootingOrder.step: IP addressing and subnet mask verification
ARP / IPv6 Neighbor Discovery (`show arp`, `show ipv6 neighbors`)
IS-IS adjacency across L1, L1/L2, or L2 links (`show isis adjacency`)
IS-IS LSP database synchronization (`show isis database`)
IS-IS route calculation and RIB installation (`show route protocol isis`)
RIB next-hop resolution and recursive loopback lookup (`show route <prefix> detail`)
FIB / Hardware Forwarding installation (`show route forwarding-table destination <prefix>`)
BGP session status andservice pseudowire (ps*) dependencies (`show bgp summary`)
End-to-end data plane testing using source-specific probes

topic.pseudowireArpNote: Step 3's ARP check for a ps* subscriber pseudowire is NOT run on the local access switch — a ps* interface lives on the PE/BNG layer. Use `show arp no-resolve interface ps<N>.<unit>` against the PE/BNG candidate devices (see routing/arp.xml's bngSubscriberResolution section for the exact device list and the ps-number-equals-unit-number rule).
topic.importantPrinciple: An IS-IS or BGP adjacency being UP does not guarantee that the required prefix is installed in the RIB or programmed into the forwarding plane (FIB).

routingTableChecks.item: Prefix existence in `inet.0` or specific VRF routing instance
Originating protocol (Direct, Static, IS-IS L1, IS-IS L2, or BGP)
Recursive next-hop resolution (e.g., resolving a BGP peer or BNG pseudowire over an IS-IS L2 loopback)
